name: Edgerun
long_description: Edgerun builds military exoskeletons. The first product is a 10-pound hip system that fits over existing kit and doubles a soldier’s range. Since April 2026, Edgerun built over a dozen iterations of their product through continuous field tests with Ukrainian fighters and secured $150M+ in LOIs. Founder David Venegas previously co-founded Durin (autonomous mining robotics) and worked at Stoke Space (at 19) and Hadrian. He is a high-school dropout, state-championship runner, adventure athlete, and pilot. Edgerun is a Y Combinator company backed by General H.R. McMaster, Cyan Banister, Joshua Steinman and Jason Miller. edgerun.com

launches.title: Edgerun: The 10 lb Military Exoskeleton
launches.tagline: Powered exoskeleton that assists every step a soldier takes under combat load
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Edgerun builds powered legs for soldiers. A 10 lb exoskeleton worn at the waist that adds assistance to every step and cuts the effort of moving under a combat load by 30-45%. Since May, we've run 100+ field tests with Ukrainian operators out of our Kyiv field office.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFLeQV2DWMc>

**▍The problem**

Every system on the modern battlefield has been upgraded. The human carrying it has not.

* For 2,500 years the soldier's load sat around 40 lbs. In the last 40 years it **doubled, then doubled again**.
* A US infantryman now carries **90-140 lbs** into a fight. The Army's own field manual sets the limit at 48 lbs.
* On deployment, load carriage causes **twice as many** evacuations as enemy contact.
* The Pentagon and VA spend **$9.3B a year** on the injuries it leaves behind.

Battles are won through speed and surprise. Load kills both.

**▍Why now**

Sixty years of military exoskeletons died the same death. The device cost more to carry than it gave back. SOCOM's TALOS burned $400M before it was cancelled in 2019.

That all changed in the last 18 months. The humanoid robotics boom produced one-pound actuators that put out 30+ Nm of torque, and 21700 cells crossed 450 Wh/kg. The components finally exist. They’re getting better every quarter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/cd255b24-3429-4270-9670-e28fc8df360b)

**▍What we built**

Our first exoskeleton is a bilateral hip system worn at the waist. It reads your gait in real time and adds torque at the moment your hip drives forward. The hip produces about 60% of the force in loaded walking, so assisting it gives the most help-per-pound of anything you could strap to the body.

* Under 10 lbs with batteries
* 30-45% less metabolic cost under a combat load
* On in 5 seconds, off in one
* 12+ hours on hot-swappable drone-class batteries
* Quasi-direct-drive actuators, composite structures, CAN bus. Nothing exotic by design.

The soldier arrives at the objective still able to fight, patrols 10 km farther, and keeps a body that lasts past one tour.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/94bf48a9-0ba6-4ce7-94a2-f467cae9657c)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/883d1e98-900a-420a-b7ff-e56cc8911c0c)

**▍Ukraine**

Our field engineers work out of a Kyiv office, alongside operators from infantry, special operations, and National Guard units who provide structured feedback every day. [Balistyka](https://balistyka.ua/), one of Ukraine's leading body armor makers, is an integration partner, helping us ensure our system fits the kit soldiers already wear.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112214&key=user_uploads/1393855/89a30d39-fe11-421c-abe7-32961da8d1bd)

**▍The mission**

Defense is the first customer, not the last. Read the mission at edgerun.com/mission
